For a point charge outside a grounded conductor we may replace the conductor by a suitable set of image charges that reproduce, in the region outside the conductor, the same electric field the real system produces.  
For a grounded conducting sphere (radius R, centre O) and a real charge q placed on the axis at a distance d (d>R) from O, the image construction is:

• Image charge q′ = –q R/d  
• Position of the image at OI = a = R²/d from O, on the line joining O to the real charge.  
• Separation between the real charge and its image  
  s = d – a = d – R²/d = (d² – R²)/d.

Because the conductor is held at zero potential, its surface charges contribute no term ρφ in the energy integral  
 U = ½ ∫ ρ φ dτ.  
Hence only the real charge appears in the sum, and the interaction energy is one-half the charge times the potential produced at its own position by the induced charges (represented by the image):

 φ_induced(at q) = k q′/s  
       = k (–q R/d)/(d – R²/d)  
       = – k q R /(d² – R²).

Therefore  

 U = ½ q φ_induced  
   = ½ q [ – k q R /(d² – R²) ]  
   = – (1/2) k q² R /(d² – R²).

Thus the net potential (interaction) energy of the charge–sphere system is

(D) U = – (1/2) k q² R / (d² – R²)

Answer: D
